children: The benchmark Dutch wholesale gas price was hovering around €79 on Thursday morning, having breached €80 in the previous trading session for the first time since January 2023.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) edged up by €0.35 to €79.60 euros per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0748 GMT, ICE data showed.
Brent crude oil remained above $100 a barrel.
Apart from the escalation in shipping attacks in the Middle East, a widening JKM-TTF spread also provided some support, said analysts at ING.

U.S. President Donald Trump said he expected the war with Iran to end after the November U.S. midterm elections and threatened again to attack a site associated with the Islamic Republic's nuclear programme after the two sides launched their biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the start of the six-month-old war.
There were also reports that Ukrainian drones hit gas processing plants in Russia’s Yamal region.

An industrial facility caught fire in Novy Urengoy, a gas-producing city in northern Russia, following a drone attack, regional Governor Dmitry Artyukhov said on Wednesday, in the first such attack on the country's natural gas hinterland.
EU gas storage stands at around 67% full, well below the five-year average of 84%.
"This leaves the market vulnerable as we head closer towards the upcoming heating season," analysts at ING said.
The British front-month gas price (NGLNMc1) was up 1.05 pence at 198.72 pence per therm.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
inched up by €0.30 to €85.87 per metric ton.
